projects.title: The Nude Party Show
projects.client: Creative direction & stage design, with Irina Shnitman
projects.short: An immersive show for the band's latest album, built around an hour of 3D-animated storytelling set inside their barn recording studio.
long: The concept was an immersive, theatrically enhanced experience for the band's latest album. The set followed a timeline of over an hour of 3D-animated storytelling inside the Barn, each part matching a song.
The barn was a deliberate choice: it is the band's recording studio in Upstate New York.

Show direction and stage design: Irina Shnitman and Nicole Girdo. 3D animation: Derek Elliott. Live video FX: Carlos Johns-Davila. Live video feed: Bryan Janiczhek. Production: Irina Shnitman and Alec Castillo. Introduction video: Alec Castillo.
projects.alt: Band performing on a red-lit stage with projected animation

projects.title: Aether House
projects.short: A semi-transparent, ghost-like house of fabric and bells hidden among the trees, which becomes a labyrinth of projected light at night.
long: Nestled quietly among the trees, Aether House emerges as a hidden discovery along the path between festival nodes. Set slightly apart from the main flow, it invites visitors to slow down, wander off the beaten path, and encounter a space of subtle sensory transformation.

The structure forms a semi-transparent, ghost-like house suspended within nature. Inside, the space is adorned with bells of varying sizes and tonalities, carefully hung inside. During the day, wind and sunlight animate the delicate facade, allowing it to breathe with its surroundings. The bells respond gently to natural rhythms: air, movement, creating an ever-changing, organic soundscape.

As night falls, the installation transforms. Imaginary patterns of light are projected onto the translucent surfaces, dissolving the boundaries between interior and exterior. Visitors are invited to step inside and get lost within a softly illuminated labyrinth of fabric, light, and sound. The bells, once passive, now react to the accidental touch of bodies moving through the space, guiding visitors intuitively through the structure and gently leading them back out into the forest.
Aether House becomes a moment of quiet immersion where nature, movement, sound, and light merge into a fleeting, dream-like experience.
projects.alt: Children and adults reaching through long translucent fabric panels in a forest

projects.title: FUNdaMental Design Build Initiative
projects.short: A performance playscape for a local art community, designed and built in two months by a team of ten students.
long: FUNdaMental, a non-profit, brings young designers together each year to build public interventions for communal benefit. Guided by studio founder Gregory Melitonov, a team of ten architecture students worked in Punta Islita over two months, from schematic design and community engagement to administration and construction.
We conceived and built a performance playscape: a multipurpose space for gatherings, shows, talks and performances that supports the PI Art Festival, held every six months.

projects.title: ELUA — Ecological Laboratory for Urban Agriculture
projects.short: Two gantry robots tend urban polyculture gardens. I took part in the architecture team: collaborating across disciplines and developing the construction drawings.
long: Idea. ELUA builds machines that adapt instead of control. Two gantry robots, one indoors and one on a sixth-floor rooftop, seed, water, weed and prune two polyculture gardens, asking whether machine-assisted cultivation can hold in an ecosystem that changes season to season.
Collaboration. The project brings together landscape architects, architects, roboticists and computer vision researchers, with community partners and local high schools.
My contribution. Developed construction drawings for the project. Collaborated across disciplines: architecture, landscape architecture, robotics and computer vision.
Project documentation and full credits: https://zihaozhang.cc/projects/elua/ (project page by Zihao Zhang).
projects.alt: Gantry robot above the rooftop garden in full growth, with solar panels and a glass pavilion behind

projects.title: Hart Island Visitor Center
projects.short: A small Welcome Center on the path between ferry dock and chapel. I developed its sustainable design solutions and helped shape the concept.
long: Part of a 20-year plan by NYC Parks for Hart Island, the city's largest public cemetery: a small Welcome Center with public restrooms and a waiting area, and a reimagined chapel as a memorial space.
The center sits on the path between ferry dock and chapel, with stone and brick masonry that echoes the chapel and a waiting area facing the water.
My contribution: sustainable design solutions, shaping the architectural concept, and fitting the building into the island's historical and natural context. Presented to NYC Parks.
projects.alt: Welcome Center rendering in a landscape

projects.title: Black Lava Fields Visitor Center
projects.short: A research-based concept that gives form to the events of the past, set in a volcanic landscape.
long: A fully research-based conceptual project that aims to materialize the events of the past, developed from research into Hiroshima Day. Entry title: Obsidian Rupture.
projects.alt: Visitor center on black lava fields

projects.title: Tushino
projects.short: Towers on wide horizontal bases that form public gardens, recalling the site's past as a paratrooper airfield.
long: Created with Steven Holl Architects, the project introduces “Parachute Hybrids”: rugged towers joined to expansive horizontal extensions at lower levels, forming vast public gardens that recall the site's past as a paratrooper airfield. Circular openings run through the buildings.
My participation: a 3D model of the environment, graphic design for drawings and presentations, and editing of sections, plans and elevations.
projects.alt: Housing towers beside a public building

projects.title: D1 Residential Complex
projects.short: A dense “vertical city” of apartments, cafés, shops and daycare, with private courtyards and a roof terrace.
long: The complex joins a compact urban layout with efficient transport access. Apartments, cafés, restaurants, a shopping center and daycare are concentrated into a “vertical city”, while private courtyards and a spacious roof terrace keep it comfortable to live in.
My participation: a 3D model of the environment, graphic design for drawings and presentations, modelling one tower facade, and a landscape diagram.
projects.alt: Black and white photo of the built residential complex

projects.title: Anti-Nuclear Protests Exhibition
projects.short: A research-based exhibition on the Hiroshima Day March. Three rooms in the Anchorage vaults stage key moments of the Manhattan Project and the Cold War through light structures.
long: A conceptual project grounded in research, meant to bring historical events to life. The semester focused on the Hiroshima Day March and its preceding events, developed into three interconnected narratives.

Three distinct rooms represent pivotal moments in the timeline, echoing the Manhattan Project and the Cold War. The narratives are told by inserting light structures into the existing rooms of the Brooklyn Bridge Anchorage.
projects.alt: Section of three vault rooms with colored light

projects.title: The Harlem Beacon
projects.short: A cultural center on a sloped triangular lot with a 15,000 sq ft performance hall and a glass ramp that doubles as billboard and exhibition space.
long: A cultural center that meets the community's needs while engaging City College students, on a triangular parking lot at West 135th Street and Amsterdam Avenue with a 15 ft height variation.

Entrances on all sides ease circulation. An exterior ramp with a double-skin glass facade serves as billboard and exhibition space. The first two floors hold entertainment areas and the performance hall; the third has classrooms, meeting spaces and a terrace with a green roof.
projects.alt: Night rendering of an event hall

projects.title: The Baptistery
projects.short: A spiral baptistery below the Geghard monastery. The sacred spring runs through the building, turning it into a filter for the human soul.
long: An extension of the ancient Geghard monastery, which sits above a cave with a sacred spring. The Baptistery stands downhill, below the Azat River, with a solid sculptural presence.

Its spiral form represents the journey of life, with water, central to baptism, as the inspiration. The spring narrows at the base before passing through the building, and additional chambers sit between the walls of the font and the facade.
projects.alt: Spiral stone baptistery on a hillside

projects.title: Development of the Little Caribbean
projects.client: Academic project, CCNY SSA, with Ornella Bonnam and Evelyn Krutoy
projects.short: Cultural infrastructure for youth at Church and Bedford Avenues, linking the Flatbush African Burial Ground to the street through a community center and shared streets.
long: The project reimagines public space at Church Avenue and Bedford Avenue and brings the historic Flatbush African Burial Ground into the urban fabric. Its aim is accessible cultural infrastructure for youth that encourages self-expression, collective identity and intergenerational connection.

Key elements: the GrowHouse community center with a demonstration kitchen, café, exhibition hall, art incubator and rooftop garden; street pavilions for commerce, art and education; terracotta forms across buildings; and a pavilion honoring the ancestors.
Studio: Just Urban Ecologies. Instructor: Ifeoma Ebo.
